messages:
anya: Heads up, we've had 5+ multi-GPU jobs fail in the last 2 hours with NCCL 'transport retry exceeded' on p2p stage. Same rack, bursty. :frowning:

matt: ugh. any pattern on job size / seq len?

anya: mostly > 16GB aggregated, long sequences, but some small jobs also hit it once they run for ~30s.

sara: can you paste the last dmesg / nccl logs?

anya: paste: ```
[ 1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0 rx_comp_timeout: cq 0x7f8f1bb0[0] did not complete
[ 1234.567895] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0 health info: err=0x17
[ 1235.001234] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0 QP 0x3f2 rc timeout, retries exhausted
NCCL WARN Call to: cudaLaunchKernel failed: unspecified launch failure
```

devon: opsbot check: were there any recent switch or NIC updates in cluster-rack-12?

opsbot: deploys: No host package updates in last 24h. Switch firmware update recorded on rack-12-tor at 02:13 UTC (fw v7.2.1 -> v7.2.3).

matt: ok switch fw bump 2am. we did some node reboots ~1:50 when rolling kernel patch. could be interplay.

lee: can we reproduce with ibv_rc_pingpong / iperf? try small message sizes and big ones.

anya: running ibv_rc_pingpong between node-a and node-b (same rack):
```
$ ibv_rc_pingpong -d mlx5_0 -s 128 -i 1
# stable up to 2K msgs, starts failing for >2K with cxg status 0x10
```

anya: iperf UDP from node-a -> node-b with 9000 MTU looks fine. but when I run udpgen with 4k payload and pps high, we see drops on mlx5 rx_crc.

sara: rx_crc is interesting. switch might be silently dropping/rewriting fragments. can you share ethtool -S counters for the mlx5 iface?

anya: ethtool -S ens192 shows: rx_crc_errors: 124, rx_errors: 130, rx_no_buf: 0, rx_fifo_errors: 0

matt: that's a lot of CRCs. which kernel/firmware on NIC?

anya: kernels are 6.1.18, mlx5 firmware 16.29.1042. opsbot says switch fw to 7.2.3 touched buffer handling code.

devon: maybe jumbo frame/fragmentation combo after fw change. did MTU change anywhere?

anya: all hosts report mtu 9000 on physical. BUT we have a bonded interface + vxlan overlay for tenant isolation. vxlan mtu is 1500 on some nodes bc ansible template wasn't applied after the kernel roll.

lee: that would fragment UDP for RoCEv2 (we use v2). fragmented UDP + switch with new fw could be dropping fragments. RoCEv2 relies on in-order UDP delivery. NCCL fatal if UDP fragments lost/out-of-order.

matt: nice find. can you confirm that ibv_rc_pingpong using RoCEv2 fails only when the effective path mtu < packet size?

anya: reproduced: setting vxlan mtu 9000 -> flows pass. set vxlan mtu 1500 -> CRCs + stash of QP timeouts. reproduction script: ```for m in 512 2048 4096 8192; do dd if=/dev/zero bs=$m count=1 | nc -u -w1 $peer 12345; done```

sara: so cause = mixed MTU due to inconsistent vxlan MTU on overlay devices introduced after reboot/ansible drift, and the new switch fw is less tolerant of fragmented RoCEv2 than old fw.

devon: mitigation? immediate and medium term?

matt: immediate: disable offloads that allow large UDP segmentation on the vxlan/NIC so RoCE uses smaller frames? alternatively set vxlan MTU consistent to 9000. Long term: pin switch fw or update all nodes and overlays.

anya: applied fix on two nodes: `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 9000` and restarted kube CNI on those hosts. reran ibv_rc_pingpong -> passes.

lee: for rollout do an ansible job to ensure vxlan MTU equals underlying phys MTU for all hosts in rack. Also add a healthcheck: run quick ibv_rc_pingpong sample during node boot to detect.

sara: also add a guard in our daemon that checks for MTU mismatch between bond/vxlan/phys and complains before scheduling multi-gpu jobs.

devon: file an infra ticket to coordinate with network team about the switch fw change. opsbot, open ticket?

opsbot: ticket created: NET-4821 "rack-12 tor fw 7.2.3 correlates with fragmented RoCEv2 drops" with priority P2.

matt: follow-up: we should add ansible step to disable GRO/TCP/UDP offloads on vxlan devices used for RoCEv2 to avoid host-level segmentation creating fragments the switch drops. Command: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off tso off`

anya: stamping notes: repro steps, ethtool outputs, fixes applied on two nodes, ticket id. I'll add to infra runbook.

sara: nice work. postmortem blurb: root cause = inconsistent overlay MTU + stricter fragment handling in switch firmware -> RoCEv2 UDP fragments dropped -> NCCL transport errors. Fix = align MTU on overlays and hosts, Ansiblize check, temporary offload toggles, and coordinate with network to validate fw. :thumbsup:

lee: can we add a prometheus alert for rx_crc_errors > 10 on mlx5 per-minute? would catch early.

matt: yes. file alert: INFRA-ALERT-rdma-rxcrc. I'll draft.
